Unit 8: The Postwar Period and Cold War (1945-1980)

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: Jackie Robinson, Brooklyn Dodgers, 1954, by Bob Sandberg, LOOK Magazine, public domain via Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: The photograph, taken in 1954, shows Jackie Robinson of the Brooklyn Dodgers, wearing cap and uniform number 42, posed ready to swing a bat. Robinson first played for the Dodgers on April 15, 1947, the first Black player in the major leagues in the twentieth century. Branch Rickey, the Dodgers' general manager, had signed Robinson from the Kansas City Monarchs of the Negro leagues in 1945.

stem: Robinson's success in 1947, when he was named National League Rookie of the Year, mattered most because it did which of the following?

options.text: It ended segregation in all American sports at once in 1947
options.misconception: Background from the books: professional football had already reintegrated in 1946, a year before Robinson's debut, and other sports integrated on their own timetables, so baseball alone did not end segregation in all sports.

options.text: It answered the claim that Black players could not compete in the majors
It proved the Negro leagues were weaker than the white leagues had been
options.misconception: Background from the books: Robinson came from the Negro leagues, so his success showed their strength, not their weakness.

options.text: It made baseball the most popular sport in the South overnight
options.misconception: Background from the books: baseball's popularity in the South did not turn on one player's award.

rationales.A: Background from the books: professional football had already reintegrated in 1946, a year before Robinson's debut, and other sports integrated on their own timetables, so baseball alone did not end segregation in all sports.
rationales.B: Background from the books: a Rookie of the Year season proved on the field that a Black player could compete, which was the claim his critics had made.
rationales.C: Robinson came from the Negro leagues, so his success showed their strength, not their weakness.
rationales.D: Baseball's popularity in the South did not turn on one player's award.
rationales.general:
1. The stimulus says Robinson was the first Black player in the majors in the twentieth century.
2. Background from the books: a first player is watched for failure, and his critics claimed Black players could not compete at that level.
3. Background from the books: Robinson won Rookie of the Year in 1947 and helped the Dodgers win the pennant.
4. Playing well answered the claim on the field, which is why the award mattered beyond baseball.
Remember: a pioneer's performance is evidence, and evidence answers a claim about ability.
